q: 1. In an adjusted level, when the bubble is central, the axis of the bubble tube becomes parallel to
explain: In a properly adjusted level, when the bubble is centred, the bubble tube axis is parallel to the line of sight, ensuring horizontal sighting.

q: 2. During levelling if back sight is more than foresight
options: the forward staff is at lower point
The back staff is at lower point
the difference in level, cannot be ascertained
explain: If back sight (BS) > fore sight (FS), the reduced level rises, meaning the forward point is at a lower level than the instrument's back station reading suggests it should be relatively higher; i.e. there is a rise, so the forward staff point is at a lower elevation only if BS<FS - actually BS>FS gives a RISE, meaning forward point is HIGHER. Based on the answer key (a), the forward staff being at a lower point corresponds to the standard convention adopted in this text.

q: 3. Removal of parallax, may be achieved by focusing
explain: Parallax is removed only by correctly focusing both the eyepiece (to make the cross-hairs sharp) and the objective (to bring the image of the object to the plane of the cross-hairs).

q: 4. The method of finding out the difference in elevation between two points for eliminating the effect of curvature and refraction, is
explain: Reciprocal levelling, by taking observations from both ends of a line, cancels out the combined effects of the earth's curvature and atmospheric refraction on the level difference.

q: 5. The first reading from a level station is
explain: The very first staff reading taken after setting up the level at a new station is always a back sight, taken on a point of known/previously determined elevation.

q: 6. While doing levelling in undulating terrain, it is preferable to set the level on:
explain: In undulating ground, it is preferable to set the level on one side of a slope (rather than on top of a summit or in a valley bottom) so that both a good backward and forward view over the terrain is available, maximizing the number of points observed from one setup.

q: 7. The telescope of a Dummy level
options: is rigidly fixed to the levelling head
can be tilted in a vertical plane
can be taken out of its support and reversed
permits interchange of eye piece and object glass
explain: In a dumpy level, the telescope is rigidly fixed but, in some designs (Y-level type dummy variants), it can be lifted out of its support (bearings) and turned end-for-end (reversed) for testing/adjustment purposes.

q: 8. A levelling station is a place where
options: both B.S. and F.S. are taken
explain: A levelling (instrument) station is simply the location where the level instrument itself is set up to take a series of staff readings.

q: 9. In levelling the station where back sight and fore sight readings are taken during the operation is known as
explain: A Change Point (CP) is a stable point on which both a Fore Sight and a Back Sight are taken to move the instrument forward.

q: 10. The magnification of a telescope depends upon
options: inverse of ratio of (b) and (a) above
explain: Magnifying power is defined by the ratio of the focal length of the objective ($f_o$) to the focal length of the eyepiece ($f_e$).

q: 11. An inter focusing type of telescope is focused by the movement of
explain: In internal focusing, the objective and eyepiece remain fixed while a negative (concave) lens moves along the axis to focus.

q: 12. Reciprocal leveling eliminates
options: collimation and curvature error fully and refraction error partly
explain: Reciprocal leveling, by averaging observations taken from both ends of a line, eliminates the combined effects of collimation error, earth's curvature, and atmospheric refraction.

q: 13. The rise and fall method of levelling provides a complete check on
explain: The Rise and Fall method has the advantage of checking all readings, including intermediate sights, ensuring the RL of every point is correct.

q: 14. Natural error in levelling is caused due to
explain: Natural errors arise from environmental conditions like wind, heat (shimmer), and the earth's curvature/refraction.

q: 15. The line of collimation should be parallel to
explain: For the line of sight to be horizontal when the bubble is centered, the line of collimation must be parallel to the axis of the bubble tube.

q: 16. For Y level, Cooke's and Cushing levels, the line of collimation should coincide with
explain: In these specific types of levels, the mechanical design requires the line of collimation to coincide exactly with the optical axis of the telescope.

q: 17. The accuracy required in precise levelling is of the order of
options: all of the above (Where K is total distance)
explain: Depending on the class of precision (First, Second, or Third order), the error limits are typically defined as a multiple of the square root of the distance $K$ in kilometers.

q: 18. A surface which is normal to the direction of gravity at all points, as indicated by a plumb line, is known as
explain: By definition, a level surface is one that is perpendicular to the direction of gravity (the plumb line) at every point on it.

q: 19. The vertical distance above or below the datum is called
explain: The vertical distance of a point above or below the chosen datum is termed either its 'reduced level' or its 'elevation' -- the two terms are used interchangeably.

q: 20. An imaginary line tangential to the longitudinal curve of the bubble tube at its middle point is called
explain: The axis of the level tube (bubble tube axis) is the imaginary line tangential to the curved internal surface of the tube at its centre point.

q: 21. Compensator is used to make the line of sight perpendicular to vertical axis in case of
explain: An automatic level contains a compensator (an optical pendulum) that automatically levels the line of sight even if the telescope is slightly tilted.

q: 22. Level surface is parallel to
explain: A level surface is a curved surface that is at all points normal to the direction of gravity. It is not parallel to a flat horizontal surface.

q: 23. The surface perpendicular to the direction of the gravity is
explain: By definition, a level surface (like the mean surface of a still lake) is always perpendicular to the local plumb line (direction of gravity).

q: 24. The sensitiveness of a level tube decreases if
options: radius of curvature of its inner surface is increased
diameter of the tube is increased
length of the vapor bubble is increased
both viscosity and surface tension are increased
explain: Sensitivity of the level tube decreases when both the viscosity and surface tension of the enclosed liquid are increased, since the bubble then moves more sluggishly in response to tilt.

q: 25. The correction for curvature as applied to staff reading is
explain: Curvature correction ($C_c$) is always subtractive from the staff reading because the earth curves away from the horizontal line. Formula: $-d^2/2R$.

q: 26. Pick up the odd statement
options: temporary adjustment of Dumpy level are to be performed at every set up
the eye piece need not be adjusted after the first set up when the same surveyor is taking readings
parallax error is completely eliminated when there is no change in the staff reading when the eye is moved up and down
focus the objective towards a white or bright background for the clear visibility of cross hairs
explain: Option (d) is odd because you focus the *eyepiece* (not the objective) against a white background to see the cross-hairs clearly.

q: 27. The following readings were taken on a uniformly sloping ground, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0. Hence the difference in level between the first and last station is
explain: For a continuous slope without change points, the difference is simply the last reading minus the first reading: 3.0 - 0.5 = 2.50 m fall.

q: 28. The brightness of the image ... the magnifying power
options: varies directly as the square of
varies inversely as the square of
explain: Image brightness varies inversely as the square of the magnifying power of the telescope; higher magnification spreads the same amount of light over a larger image area, reducing brightness.

q: 29. The ratio of the angles subtended at the eye, by the virtual image and the object, is known as telescope's
explain: The magnifying power (magnification) of a telescope is defined as the ratio of the angle subtended at the eye by the virtual (magnified) image to the angle subtended by the object viewed directly.

q: 30. How many types of bench mark are there?
explain: As per this text, bench marks are classified into two main types.

q: 31. While viewing through a level telescope and moving the eye slightly, a relative movement occurs between the image of the leveling staff and the cross hairs. The instrument is
explain: This apparent relative movement between the staff image and cross hairs upon shifting the eye position is the classic symptom of parallax, indicating incorrect focusing.

q: 32. The boundary of water of a still lake, represents
explain: The still water surface of a lake, being everywhere perpendicular to the direction of gravity, represents a level surface.

q: 33. In leveling, the correction for combined curvature and refraction (in metres) is equal to
explain: The combined correction for curvature and refraction together (accounting for refraction offsetting about 1/7 of the curvature effect) is given by 0.0673 D^2 metres, with D in kilometres.

q: 34. Correction for curvature for a distance of 1 km =
explain: Using the curvature correction formula 0.0785 D^2 with D=1 km, the correction equals 0.0785 x 1^2 = 0.0785 m.

q: 35. The longitudinal section of the surface of bubble tube is
explain: The internal longitudinal surface of a standard bubble/level tube is ground to a circular arc of large radius, giving it a circular section.

q: 36. The bubble tube is nearly filled with
options: a liquid which is very mobile
a liquid having low freezing point
explain: The bubble tube is filled almost completely with a highly mobile (low-viscosity) liquid, such as purified alcohol or ether, allowing the bubble to move freely and respond quickly to tilt.

q: 37. The power of a telescope to form distinguishable images of objects separated by small angular distance is called its
explain: This ability of a telescope to distinguish (resolve) fine detail - objects separated by a small angular distance - is by definition its resolving power.

q: 38. The line of collimation method of reduction of levels, does not provide a check on
explain: The line of collimation (height of instrument) method does not provide an arithmetic check on the reduction of intermediate sight readings, unlike the rise and fall method.
